bgp: NONE — this network runs no BGP; out of scope entirely

nets.derivationRule: system-ID = BCD packing of router-id: zero-pad each octet to 3 decimal digits, concatenate to 12 digits, regroup into three 4-digit chunks

topologyScope: 2 nodes, 1 point-to-point link. A 3-node triangle was authored but SHELVED (does not fit prod host / cEOS unbootable off-host) — no transit-path preference story this round.

parityCriteria.scope: At G2 (post-P1 harvest): every prefix OSPF advertises must be present in each device's IS-IS link-state database, with a next-hop identical to the one OSPF resolves
parityCriteria.tolerance: zero — no missing or extra prefixes
parityCriteria.compareAgainst: the link-state database (LSDB) — NEVER the routing table/RIB, because IS-IS routes are computed but not installed during coexistence by design; a RIB-based comparison reads empty on a perfectly healthy fabric

targetProtocol.level: level-2-only — EOS token is `is-type level-2`; there is NO `level-2-only` token
targetProtocol.metricStyle: wide — EOS platform default, NO `metric-style` command exists on this platform; state it in packages, never configure it
targetProtocol.instanceIdentifierNote: Identical on both devices per requirements ('any consistent value' is explicitly permitted, not derivable — see Assumptions).

platformDialect.canonicalStanza: router isis <instance> / net <NET> / is-type level-2 / ! / address-family ipv4 unicast / ! / interface <Ethernet-if> / isis enable <instance> / isis network point-to-point / isis metric <value> / ! / interface Loopback0 / isis enable <instance> / isis passive

preferencePolicy.rollback: `no distance <value>` under the same address-family stanza (reverts to EOS default 115) — single knob, seconds-reversible

shiftMechanism.note: Any value < 110 (OSPF's AD) achieves the flip; 90 is this plan's proposed value, not a derived constant — see Assumptions & Open Questions.
shiftMechanism.location: under `router isis <instance>` -> `address-family ipv4 unicast` -> `distance <value>` (NOT at the router-isis top level — EOS rejects that placement)

preferencePolicy.coexistencePhase: OSPF-learned routes remain preferred on every device while both protocols run. EOS default administrative distances already satisfy this (OSPF 110 < IS-IS 115) — no explicit distance command required in P1.

metricTranslation.rule: each IS-IS interface metric equals the harvested OSPF interface cost on that same interface — the cost relationship is carried forward exactly
metricTranslation.loopback0: isis enable <instance> + isis passive only — canonical stanza carries no isis metric line on Loopback0
metricTranslation.scopeNote: Two devices, one link → no alternate path exists. A clean pass proves faithful per-interface metric translation only, NOT path-selection preference preservation (the 3-node form of this check is not exercisable this round).
